content:
Facts: Deceased's children challenged validity of wife's 2006 holographic will allegedly appointing husband sole heir (produced only as photocopy, original never found), claiming it revoked 2001 public will leaving husband usufruct bequest in lieu of legitimate portion with religious province as universal heir; alternatively, claimed right to renounce father's usufruct bequest exercising Art. 551 option asserting legitimate portion rights; subordinately, requested taking over usufruct bequest as father's heirs.
Legal Framework: Articles 536-537, 551, 649, 666, 698, 979 Italian Civil Code (legitimate heirs; legacy in lieu of legitimate portion; automatic legacy acquisition; alternative legacy choice transfer; successive usufruct; usufruct extinction); Arts. 2724-2725 (testimonial proof limitations for lost documents); case law on photocopy wills (Cass. 22191/2020, 6918/2019, 10171/2015).
Interpretive Issues: Evidentiary sufficiency of unauthenticated photocopy when original holographic will unavailable; presumptions arising from original's disappearance; whether legacy in lieu of legitimate portion acquired automatically or requires acceptance; transferability to heirs of Art. 551 renunciation option; whether deceased's children qualify as legitimate heirs entitled to reduction action when claiming through spouse-predecessor (not child-descendant); usufruct transmissibility to beneficiary's heirs absent testamentary successive-usufruct provision.
Principles Applied: Unavailable holographic will with existence proven only by informal copy equivalent to destruction creating revocation presumption; burden on interested party proving destruction by third party or accidental loss or testator's non-revocation intent absent party's contribution to disappearance. Photocopy conformity verification impossible when original unproduced; copy unsuitable proving original existence absent circumstances overcoming revocation presumption (destruction by others, accident, testator non-intent). Generic allegations (neighbor delivery without identification) insufficient overcoming revocation presumption or proving non-testator destruction. Legacy in lieu of legitimate portion acquired ipso iure per Art. 649 without acceptance requirement; prevailing opinion confirmed by Cass. SU 7098/2011. Legitimate heir receiving tacit bequest may renounce obtaining lawful share; power included in reduction action right (Art. 536); requires renunciation obligation (written ad substantiam for immovables, informal/conclusive for others) prior to or simultaneous with reduction request. Transfer occurred upon testator's death; no renunciation by legatee before death; awareness condition met (witness confirmed knowledge). Art. 666 alternative-legacy choice-transfer mechanism inapplicable; concerns different case where transfer conditional upon choice whereas ordinary legacy transfers immediately. Art. 536(3) reserves rights exclusively for direct descendants; reduction action available only to children and children's descendants, not spouse's descendants. Spouse's children claiming as spouse's descendants cannot exercise spouse's reduction rights against spouse's estate. Usufruct extinguishes upon usufructuary's death per Art. 979(1); no successive usufruct provision per Art. 698; taking-over claim unfounded introducing different thema decidendum from writ.
